IS: 2896 -1978 

Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR WOODEN HANDLES 
FOR CARPENTERS 5 AUGERS 

(First Revision) 

0. FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Indian 
Standards Institution on 19 January 1978, after the draft finalized by 
the Timber Stores Sectional Committee had been approved by the Civil 
Engineering Division Council. 

0.2 The general requirements for wooden tool handles are covered by 
IS : 620-1975*. A series of Indian Standards have been prepared for 
various hand tools and for use with these hand tools, a series of standards 
for corresponding wooden handles have been prepared. This standard 
deals with wooden handles for carpenters' augers conforming to 
IS : 2852-1964f. 

0.3 This standard was first published in 1965. In this revision, based on 
the experience gained in the use of the standard, modifications have been 
incorportated in the defects permitted for blanks for the handle. 

0.4 In the formulation of this standard due weightage has been given to 
international co-ordination among the standards and practices prevailing 
in different countries in addition to relating it to the practices in the 
field in this country. 

0.5 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this 
standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, 
expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in 
accordance with IS : 2-1960J. The number of significant places retained 
in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified 
value in this standard. 



1. SCOPE 

1.1 This standard covers the requirements of wooden handles for 
carpenters' augers conforming to IS : 2852-1964f. 

♦Specification for general requirements for wooden tool handles ( third revision ). 

^Specification for carpenters' augers. 

JRules for rounding off numerical values ( revised). 



IS : 2896 - 1978 

2. TERMINOLOGY 

2.1 For the purpose of this standard, the definitions given in IS : 620- 
1975* shall apply. 

3. SPECIES OF TIMBER 

3.1 The handles for carpenters' augers shall be manufactured from any 
of the timbers specified for Class V handles in IS : 620-1975*. 

3.2 The blanks shall be well-seasoned (preferably air-seasoned) to a 
moisture content not exceeding 15 percent and not less than 8 percent. 
They shall be free from centre heart ( pith ), any kind of decay ( rot ), 
in ect attack, checks, shakes, splits (except hair splits ), borer holes, 
warp and any other defect except those permitted in the finished handles 
(see IS: 620-1975*). 

4. MANUFACTURE 

4.1 The handles shall be manufactured from seasoned and selected blanks 
and shaped as shown in Fig. 1. Handles of other forms may be fitted to 
any of the tools by arrangement between the manufacturer and the 
purchaser, 

4.2 It is recommended that, immediately after manufacture, the handles 
be dipped in raw linseed oil at room temperature, as this treatment 
retards changes in moisture content. 

5. DIMENSIONS AND TOLERANCES 

5.1 Dimensions — Handles shall conform to the dimensions as shown 
in Fig. 1. 

5.2 Tolerances — The following tolerances shall be permissible: 

a) Where the head of the tool fits { ~ mm 

b) At other places ±2 mm 

6. OTHER REQUIREMENTS 

6.1 Workmanship and finish, permissible defects ( in addition to those 
given in 3.2 ), tests, treatment and sampling shall be as specified in 
IS : 620-1975*. 



♦Specification for general requirements for wooden tool handles ( third revision ),

7. MARKING 

7.1 Unless otherwise specified, each handle shall be legibly and indelibly 
marked with the manufacturer's name, initials or recognized trade-mark 
and the year of manufacture. In addition, the size of the carpenters' 
augers for which the handle is required shall also be marked. 

7.1.1 The handle may also be marked with the ISI Certification 
Mark. 

Note — The use of the ISI Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the 
Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Marks ) Act and the Rules and Regu- 
lations made thereunder. The ISI Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard 
conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements 
of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality 
control which is devised and supervised by ISI and operated by the producer. ISI 
marked products are also continuously checked by ISI for conformity to that standard 
as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of 
the ISI Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, may be 
obtained from the Indian Standards Institution.
